types.standards_anchor: ANSI/NETA ATS switchgear and switchboard assemblies: nameplate data compared with drawings and specifications; bus continuity and rating; interrupting rating; insulation resistance phase-to-phase and phase-to-ground; contact/pole resistance; ground and bonding verification; interlock operation and sequencing confirmed correct; protective device settings as-left. Medium-voltage assemblies add power-frequency withstand.
types.note: held to 13 fields; medium-voltage power-frequency withstand and detailed device-by-device settings tables are left out on purpose - they belong in a dedicated test record referenced by the checklist, not squeezed into the nameplate. If this switchgear register includes medium-voltage gear, a follow-up field for withstand test result may be worth adding once that's confirmed rather than assumed here.

types.standards_anchor: ANSI/NETA ATS switchboard assemblies, as switchgear but distribution-scale: nameplate vs drawings; main and bus ratings; interrupting rating; insulation resistance; bolted-connection torque; ground bus bonding; metering and instrument transformer complement.
types.note: Kept to items a NETA-style acceptance record and a nameplate/drawing comparison actually expects; left out things like feeder breaker schedules or full one-line detail as belonging to drawings rather than a single nameplate table.

types.standards_anchor: ANSI/NETA ATS motor control centres: nameplate vs drawings; bus rating; each starter/unit size and type; overload element rating and setting; control voltage; insulation resistance; interlock and control-circuit function. The record is per ASSEMBLY, with the unit complement counted rather than enumerated - individual starters are not their own type (variant rule).
types.note: Kept to assembly-level fields per the standards anchor's variant rule - individual starters/overload settings are not enumerated here as they belong to the per-unit sub-record, not the MCC nameplate itself. Short Circuit Withstand and Enclosure Rating are left out of 'installed' since they aren't independently re-verified in the field beyond the shop drawing confirmation.

fields.reasoning: the nameplate/system voltage NETA ATS records against the drawing rating

nameplate frequency, standard field left unswapped per convention

presence/type of GF protection scheme, a functional attribute the anchor expects on the record

types.standards_anchor: ANSI/NETA ATS adjustable-speed drives, with the drive as a commissioned unit in its own right: nameplate vs drawings; input and output voltage/current; horsepower or kW rating; bypass arrangement; line reactor or filter; programmed acceleration/deceleration and min/max speed as-left; control signal type. NOTE the boundary: the `pump` VFD yes/no field answers "does this pump have one", which is a different question.
types.note: Left acceleration/deceleration time without a unit field rather than guessing seconds-vs-minutes convention; a reviewer can add unit if the firm's forms standardize on one. Did not add a stand-alone 'HP' field alongside kW since the anchor treats horsepower/kW as one rating and Ontario nameplates typically print both together.

fields.reasoning: nameplate vs drawings per NETA ATS acceptance
output side, distinct from input for VFDs
the duty the drive is sized to drive; kW is the shared metric figure, HP commonly co-appears on the nameplate itself so no imperial swap needed for the field label

e.g. 4-20mA, 0-10V, BAS network — what the drive actually takes as-left

types.standards_anchor: ANSI/NETA ATS uninterruptible power systems: nameplate vs drawings; kVA/kW rating; input and output voltage and configuration; battery type, string voltage and cell/block count; rated autonomy at load; bypass arrangement (static and maintenance); alarm and monitoring complement. Autonomy VERIFIED is a timed test result - keep the field to the RATING and let the test record hold the reading.
types.note: Kept to the NETA-anchored electrical facts plus the battery string particulars; left out enclosure/environmental details and a full alarm-point list as specification-drawing concerns rather than nameplate fields - easy to add if this project's checklist wants them.

types.standards_anchor: ASME BPVC Section IV/VIII marking for the vessel where applicable, plus CSA/AHRI water-heater rating conventions: storage volume, input rating and energy source, recovery rate at a stated temperature rise, thermostat and high-limit settings, T&P relief valve rating. For indirect/semi-instantaneous units the heating-medium side matters as much as the domestic side.
types.note: 13 fields — the anchor's storage/input/recovery/setpoint/relief set plus the two energy-source qualifiers (Gas Type, Heating Medium) that will sit blank on units they don't apply to. Left Recovery Rate metric-only, matching the pump Flow-field precedent, rather than guessing at an imperial convention the sibling tables don't establish.

fields.reasoning: Gas, electric, steam or indirect-fired — governs which other fields on the nameplate actually apply
Natural gas vs propane where the unit is gas-fired; parallels the boiler vocabulary
Tank capacity is the basic sizing fact and the figure both the spec and nameplate carry
The AHRI/CSA rated heat input the schedule specifies and the nameplate confirms
Rated recovery at the stated temperature rise, the core performance figure the CSA/AHRI rating anchors on
Recovery rate is meaningless without the rise it was measured at; both figures travel together on the rating plate
Field-set control temperature, read at the unit during verification

The rated efficiency figure the spec calls for and the submittal confirms
Domestic hot/cold connection size, read directly off the shop drawing and confirmed at the unit
Applies to indirect/semi-instantaneous units where a boiler loop rather than direct fire supplies the heat

types.standards_anchor: Manufacturer and CSA B483-family conventions for potable water treatment: service flow rate and pressure drop, resin volume and exchange capacity, regeneration type and control (time/meter), brine tank capacity and salt setting, hardness in and out. NOTE: the anchor here is weaker than the NETA and ASME ones - flag any field that is firm convention rather than standard.
types.note: Anchor here is manufacturer/CSA B483 convention rather than a hard test standard, so several fields (salt dose, configuration) are flagged in their own reasoning as firm/trade convention rather than a cited requirement. Exchange capacity kept in kgr on purpose - that's how the trade writes it in both unit systems, same pattern as CFM/MBH. Left out ancillary items (bypass valve, sample ports) as spec-drawing concerns rather than nameplate data anyone would record on site.

fields.reasoning: the rated continuous flow the softener is sized to treat; spec sets it, shop drawing confirms the selection, installed is what's actually piped
governs whether the softener fits the system's available head; a nameplate/curve value confirmed at startup
the bed size that sets exchange capacity between regenerations

time-clock vs. meter-initiated vs. demand - determines how the unit is expected to behave day to day
the specific controller/valve model or logic driving regeneration, distinct from the type
sizes how long the unit runs unattended between salt fills
a startup setting rather than a spec requirement in most projects - convention, not standard
the design basis and the measured value the softener is actually sized against
the performance target and the value confirmed at commissioning - the softener's whole job stated as a number
inlet/outlet size, already written the same convention in either system
simplex, duplex-alternating, or twin-tank - affects whether treated water is ever interrupted during regeneration, worth recording as installed
the vessel's working pressure limit, checked against the system's actual operating pressure

types.standards_anchor: CSA B64 series (backflow preventers and vacuum breakers) with CSA B64.10 field testing: device TYPE designation (RP/RPDA, DCVA/DCDA, PVB/SVB), size, hazard classification (severe/moderate) and the cross-connection it protects, installation orientation and clearance, relief port discharge arrangement. The annual test READINGS are test-record data; the nameplate carries the device identity and its ratings.
types.note: Left out annual test readings (test-cock pressure differentials, etc.) deliberately - those are B64.10 test-record data, not nameplate content, and belong to a separate test form. Body material and strainer presence are real but marginal; cut them to keep this at 12 rather than pad toward 15.

fields.reasoning: CSA B64 identifies backflow preventers by assembly type first; the record must confirm the type installed matches what the spec required
line size drives every other rating on the assembly and is read directly off the body
CSA B64 selection depends on the hazard degree of the cross-connection, set at spec stage and confirmed against the assembly proposed
the standard requires the record to state what the device protects, not just what the device is
duty the specification stated and the submittal confirms; flow is one of the two quantities that genuinely swap units between systems
pressure rating governs assembly selection and is stated on the nameplate and the schedule alike
distinguishes potable-water assemblies from hot-water-rated variants; a spec-stage requirement
most RP/PVB assemblies are orientation-restricted (horizontal only, or minimum height above grade); the field record confirms what was actually built
CSA B64 installation requirements set a minimum clearance for relief-valve discharge and access; only meaningful once installed
flanged, threaded or grooved changes the field verification and maintenance access, and is visible at the unit
the anchor calls out relief port discharge specifically; how it is piped or air-gapped is a field-verifiable fact distinct from the device rating
the CSA B64 designation on the assembly is a requirement reference, not firm branding, and is what the spec and submittal both cite

types.standards_anchor: ASME BPVC Section VIII for the receiver (stamp, MAWP, volume) plus compressor rating conventions: type (reciprocating/rotary screw/scroll), free air delivery at a stated discharge pressure, motor rating, duty/control mode (load-unload, modulating, VSD), and the air-treatment train (dryer type, dewpoint, filtration). For medical or laboratory air the purity and alarm requirements govern - flag if unknown for this project.
types.note: 13 fields — reciprocating/rotary-screw plant air is the assumed case. Medical or laboratory air purity and alarm requirements are governed by a different standard (CSA Z7396 / NFPA 99) and are not covered here; flag if this project's air compressor serves medical or lab air, since that would add fields (alarm setpoints, purity monitoring) rather than fit inside this set.

fields.reasoning: reciprocating, rotary screw or scroll — governs everything else on this table

the CRN or ASME stamp number recorded off the vessel itself

the treatment-train performance value the standard's record expects
oil-free rating or ISO 8573-1 class where stated

types.standards_anchor: Hydronic/plumbing pump rating conventions as for `pump`, plus the sump-specific content a commissioning record needs: simplex or duplex arrangement, alternator, float/level control type and set points (start, stop, high-level alarm), basin size, discharge size and check/isolation arrangement, and whether the pump is on emergency power. Capacity is stated at a duty point (flow at head).
types.note: kept to 13 - no Voltage/Phase field; Motor Power is the only electrical rating a sump pump's small single-phase motor usually needs on record, and adding voltage/phase would duplicate what the panel schedule already carries.

fields.reasoning: simplex or duplex is the first thing a spec calls for and the installed pit confirms

a life-safety-adjacent setpoint the anchor names explicitly and FPT must confirm
